## Disposition

The extension from a degreewise finite polynomial resolution on finite
free integer lattices to all abelian groups is kernel-checked. This
is a reduction of the remaining existence problem, not a construction
of an inhabitant of the finite-lattice resolution type.

The input is the explicit LatticeBD structure in the required lifted
coefficient universe. The output LatticeBD.toUniversalBD supplies the
actual natural augmentation and differentials, their identities,
epimorphic augmentation and categorical exactness in every degree.

The canonical comparison is the existing protected endpoint of 038:
canonicalUnit_allShifts_of_LatticeBD is obtained by applying that
endpoint to the constructed UniversalBD package. Parent PR #3845
merged at 5dd36e28545e13e7b654454ad047911e21a824f3.

## Construction

For a polynomial functor

$$
P(A)=\bigoplus_{j=1}^{k}\mathbb Z[A^{r_j}],
$$

a natural map on finite free lattices extends uniquely to all
modules. Each tuple is the image of the generic tuple in the
appropriate finite free lattice. The formula applies the target
functor to this tuple map and the value on the generic tuple.
Naturality and the restriction identity are checked on free
generators. Injectivity of restriction implies that the augmentation
and differential identities on the lattices extend to the whole
module category.

Every polynomial element of an arbitrary free module involves a
finite union of finite supports of basis vectors. A finite-coordinate
retraction fixes the element. Exactness on finite free modules
therefore gives exactness on free modules of arbitrary rank.

## 41. Enlarging the field without losing the cohomological bound

SLayer makes the hypotheses of the preceding arithmetic and homological estimates available for an arbitrary base field satisfying HasMuQ. This condition requires a primitive root of order $\ell$ for odd primes, and of order four at the prime two. It guarantees a procyclic cyclotomic image.

The independent restriction argument is especially short. Every finite cyclotomic enlargement $L'/L$ has the same infinite cyclotomic extension and hence the same cyclotomic kernel $U_\infty$. A global class that vanishes on the absolute Galois group of $L'$ vanishes upon restriction to this kernel. Injectivity of restriction to the kernel, proved in the preceding section, makes the original class zero. Restriction preserves the local coboundary conditions on decomposition and inertia groups. Therefore the Sha module of $L$ injects into that of $L'$, and its length cannot decrease on enlargement.

The submitted proof uses a related dual description. The common module of admissible characters on the kernel has twisted cyclotomic action. Inflation-restriction and local procyclic vanishing identify the Sha modules with its invariant submodules at successive layers. Algebraic duality with the injective cogenerator $\mathbb Q_\ell/\mathbb Z_\ell$ identifies their lengths with the lengths of cokernels of $T^{\ell^m}-1$, for one common dual operator $T$. This argument does not require a finite-rank module. The factorization $T^d-1=(T-1)\sum_{i=0}^{d-1}T^i$ gives a surjection of the larger-layer cokernel onto the original one. This independently reconstructs the source's sha_le mechanism, while original formal descent and local comparison remain replay obligations.

## 40. Why a uniform finite-layer bound controls global cohomology

The actual invariant shaInv is the module length of a subgroup of continuous first Galois cohomology with coefficients $\mathbb Q_\ell/\mathbb Z_\ell(-E)$. The negative twist means that the action is multiplication by the inverse cyclotomic character to the power $E$. The local conditions require vanishing on decomposition groups above $\ell$ and on inertia groups elsewhere. It is not the unrestricted first cohomology group.

Let $L_\nu=L(\mu_{\ell^\nu})$ and let $U_\nu$ be its absolute Galois subgroup inside the absolute Galois group of $L$. Their intersection is $U_\infty$, the kernel of the full cyclotomic character. Under TopRoot, the cyclotomic image is the principal group $1+\ell^c\mathbb Z_\ell$: it is closed, lies in this group and not in its next principal subgroup. The principal group is topologically cyclic (with the additional source condition $c\ge2$ at the prime two).

Restriction to $U_\infty$ is injective on first cohomology. Indeed, a cocycle vanishing there descends to the procyclic quotient. Multiplication by the nonzero scalar $\chi(\gamma)^{-E}-1$ on $\mathbb Q_\ell/\mathbb Z_\ell$ is surjective, so subtract a coboundary making the cocycle zero at a topological generator. The cocycle identity and continuity make it zero everywhere. On the cyclotomic kernel the action is trivial, so the restricted cocycle is an additive character, independent of the representative of its cohomology class. The local coboundary conditions imply vanishing on the relevant intersections, and the cocycle identity gives equivariance under conjugation.

## 39. The arithmetic cancellation: two ways to count one group

The preceding bound grows with the modulus $Q=\ell^\nu$. The source SCount removes that growth by counting an intermediate finite group of divisor relations in two different ways.

Use additive notation $Y=F^\times$, $I=\mathrm{Div}(F)$, $d_F=\mathrm{div}$, and $T=\mu(F)$. Let $a=(1+\ell^c)^E$, $n=\ell^{\nu-c}$, and $\delta=g-a$, $\delta_I=g_I-a$ for the compatible inverse Galois actions on elements and divisors. Since $g_I^n=1$ and the divisor group is torsion-free, $\delta_I$ is injective. Put $U=d_F^{-1}(\delta_I I)$, $W=U/(\delta Y+T)$, $EQ=\ker d_F/(\delta\ker d_F+T)$ and $ClQ=I/(d_F Y+\delta_I I)$.

The unique divisor solving $\delta_I D=d_F y$ for $y\in U$ gives a map from $W$ to the kernel of the twisted endomorphism of the ideal class group. Its kernel is precisely $EQ$. The class group is finite and an endomorphism of a finite group has equal kernel and cokernel orders. Hence $|W|=|EQ||ClQ|$. The desired equivariant characters are homomorphisms from $ClQ$ to the residue coefficient ring, so their number is bounded by the order of its primary part.

The equivariant Dirichlet logarithmic lattice identifies the free unit group with a full lattice in the sum-zero hyperplane of the infinite-place coordinates. The Galois permutation consists of $r=r_2(L)$ cycles of length $n$. The full determinant of $g-a$ has absolute value $(a^n-1)^r$. Remove the constant coordinate line, on which the operator acts by $1-a$. The lattice index is exactly

$$
|EQ|(a-1)=(a^n-1)^r.
$$

Writing $v=v_\ell(E)$, lifting the exponent gives $v_\ell(a-1)=c+v$ and $v_\ell(a^n-1)=\nu+v$. Thus $v_\ell(|EQ|)=r(\nu+v)-c-v$. The unit determinant supplies precisely the layer-dependent factor needed in the count.
